subject: Invoice handoff & post-sale billing setup for Apex Analytics
messages:
From: Lynn Morales <lynn@apexanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@apexanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice handoff & post-sale billing setup for Apex Analytics

Hi Ben —

Great to have the contract signed — thanks for working with our legal team. We have a couple quick billing items to finalize so we can route our initial purchase order and kick off payments: 

1) Preferred invoice delivery: we typically accept e-invoices via SFTP/XML integration for our AP system, but smaller vendors sometimes send a PDF copy to procure@apexanalytics.com. Can Redwood support either? Which do you prefer for first invoice?

2) Billing contact: please confirm who will be the day-to-day billing contact we should loop in for PO and payment reconciliation.

3) VAT/tax: we operate across US + EU entities and will need the invoice to include VAT tagging where applicable. Do you need our VAT IDs for each entity now or can that wait until billing goes live?

If it helps, I can share a sample PO and target remit information once we align on delivery method. Looking to get the first invoice out this week so AP can process the payment.

Thanks —
Lynn Morales\VP, Finance Operations\Apex Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Morales <lynn@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice handoff & post-sale billing setup for Apex Analytics

Hi Lynn —

Thanks — congrats again on closing with legal. We support both delivery methods you described; here are the pros/cons and a suggested path for a smooth first invoice: 

- Portal / API (recommended long-term): structured e-invoice (XML/UBL) over SFTP or webhook. Better for automated matching and VAT tagging. If you can share SFTP credentials or an API endpoint we’ll push a sample e-invoice.
- Email PDF (fastest first invoice): we can send a PDF to procure@apexanalytics.com and cc a billing contact for records. Good as a short-term fallback while integrations are provisioned.

What I need from you to proceed this week: 
- Billing contact name + email for the invoice (who should we send the PDF to, or who will own the SFTP credentials?)
- PO number to place on the invoice (if available)
- VAT IDs for the entities that will be billed (you can send these to me or to procure@apexanalytics.com)

Attached: redwood-invoice-sample.pdf (PDF) and billing-onboarding-checklist.csv (spreadsheet) — the checklist shows required fields for the e-invoice XML and a minimal mapping if you take the SFTP route.

Proposed next steps: 
1) If you want the first invoice as a PDF this week, reply with billing contact + PO and we’ll issue the PDF to procure@apexanalytics.com today.
2) If you prefer SFTP/XML, Connor can share the enrollment invite and token and we’ll schedule a 30-minute handoff to validate the XML mapping.

I’ll hold on whichever you pick — thanks, Lynn.

Best,
Ben Carter\Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lynn Morales <lynn@apexanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice handoff & post-sale billing setup for Apex Analytics

Hi Lynn — looping in a couple technical details from our AP team to make the XML/SFTP route easier if you choose it.

Key notes: 
- We support UBL 2.1 XML and a simplified vendor-specific schema (attached: e-invoice-xml-schema-v2.1.xml). The checklist Ben attached maps our fields to common AP fields (invoice number, invoice date, PO, line-level tax tags).
- For SFTP we can deliver either to your inbound folder or a dedicated vendor path. We prefer SFTP keys (scoped) but can do username/password on first pass.
- If your AP system requires split invoices across entities (bill-to vs remit-to), include entity identifiers in the PO and we’ll emit separate invoices per entity. Provide the VAT IDs and the target accounting codes and we’ll map them in the feed.

Operational ask: can you share a contact who can accept a test file (SFTP credentials or API sandbox endpoint)? If you want to go the email route first, we’ll send the PDF and then follow up with a short integration window (typically 48–72 hours) to validate the XML mapping.

HubSpot deal link (internal): https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DF-2026-874

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the XML if helpful.

-Marissa\Director, Billing Operations\Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lynn Morales <lynn@apexanalytics.com>, procure@apexanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice handoff & post-sale billing setup for Apex Analytics

Hi all — quick operational note from the portal/enrollment side: 

- I’ve created a portal enrollment invite for Apex Analytics and attached the one-click invite HTML (portal-enroll-invite.html). The invite will create a vendor profile and generate a scoped API token for automated invoice pushes.
- If Apex wants an immediate PDF this week while the portal is provisioned, Ben — go ahead and issue the PDF. I’ll schedule the XML test once we have credentials (proposed window: Wed 11/25 10:00–10:30 PT).

Action items we’ll take from here: 
1) Ben to issue PDF invoice to procure@apexanalytics.com if Lynn confirms PO now.
2) Lynn (or procurement) to share SFTP creds or accept the portal invite for the XML onboarding.
3) Marissa to validate VAT tags once Lynn shares the VAT IDs for the billed entities.

Connor O'Brien\Billing Integrations Engineer\Redwood Inference
